        Before you read the tea leaves

        Killmails only tell half the story.

        Every number GoSleuth shows comes from killmails, and a killmail is only written when something dies. Nothing is recorded for the ships that warped off, the fights that ended with no losses, or the half of a battle on the other side of a gate or wormhole.

        That's survivorship bias turned inside out: you see only the losses, never the ones who got away. Some things never appear on a killmail at all:

        • Objectives. A fight that cost 3B ISK to save a 20B Keepstar looks like a loss.
        • Logistics. Logi pilots who kept everyone alive aren't listed, despite our requests.
        • Fights with no deaths. If nothing died, it never happened as far as the data knows.

        GoSleuth gathers what the killmails show and lays it out clearly. Interpreting it is up to you. Treat what you see as clues, not conclusions.

        About GoSleuth

        EVE GoSleuth

        What it is

        So... is this some sort of zKill browser?

        GoSleuth is an EVE Online intel tool. Give it a pilot, corporation, alliance, or system and it pulls their killmails from zKillboard, then lays them out to be easily read: who they fly with, where and when they are active, what they fly, the battles they have been in, and more.

        Use it to find a pilot's alts and associates, size up a corporation or alliance, or learn who lives in a system.

        In the grand tradition of Pyfa being written in Python, GoSleuth is written in Go.

        GoSleuth will always be free, open source, free of ads, subscriptions, paid feature tiers, ect. This app runs entirely in your local environment and connects to no servers beyond the standard apis that are listed in the Data Sources. This app strives to maintain your privacy - if you feel that it is not for some reason, please submit a bug report using the button below.

        If you feel this app has been worth your time, feel free to - with no obligation or expectation - donate some Isk or Plex to in game.

        Author

        I'm just a guy who likes data.

        I'm , known in game as , and sometimes known around J-space as "The Spreadsheet Guy".

        I am a developer by trade, having coded for much of my life. I love to dabble in tools for EVE, having built many a small thing here or there to give myself or my corpmates some cool tools to use. GoSleuth is something I've been working on for many years, and it has had many iterations.

        AI disclosure

        Unfortunately coded with Claude Opus 5.5

        Before GoSleuth, I wrote a tool in Python I called eve-info. My corporation and I used it internally, and it had pretty much all the same functionality GoSleuth has. I wrote that tool entirely by hand, and it worked. I knew I wanted to port it to Go, to take advantage of its asynchronous goroutines and its much better speed in general.

        I wrote GoSleuth's original backend by hand, about 2,600 lines of Go. Everything added after Oct 24th, 2026, the whole interface included, was built with Claude, an AI coding assistant, under my direction.

        I would estimate that at this time, about 25% of the backend (not GUI or test related) is either my code or based heavily on my code. This number will undoubtedly decrease as I release more updates utilizing Claude Opus 5.5.

        I am no fan of AI or how it is used today, and the README explains why I used it anyway. If you would rather not use AI assisted software, I completely understand.

        Have you generated a Debug of a faulty search?

        A debug log of a faulty search is the best way to help us diagnose a bug. To make one:

        1. Open Preferences at the top right, then Advanced
        2. Tick Debug mode and Save
        3. Run the faulty search again
        4. Back in Preferences > Advanced, Open debug folder and attach the newest zip to your report

            Clear the cache?

            Anything cleared is looked up again from the ESI when next needed, so the next searches will be slower. This can not be undone.

            Most of the cache keeps itself fresh: pilots, corporations and alliances are looked up again after 24 hours, and ships, systems and other game data with each EVE data release. Killmails never change, so they are kept until cleared.
